title: Next Bigger Around the Ring
statement:
You get an array nums that is arranged in a ring: after the last element, the walk continues from the first one.

For each position i, walk forward around the ring starting just after i and find the first value that is strictly greater than nums[i]. Return an array of those values, with -1 where no greater value exists anywhere in the ring.

examples.why: For 4, the walk goes 1, then wraps to 3, then 8. For 1, wrapping reaches 3 first. 8 is the largest, so it gets -1.
Equal values do not count. The answer needs a strictly greater value.
Only the 3 at the end needs to wrap around, and it finds the 6 at the start.

hints: Without the ring, this is the classic "next greater element". How does a stack solve that in one pass?
Wrapping around means a value near the end may find its answer near the start. What if you walked the array twice?

Loop i from 0 to 2n − 1 and use index i mod n. Keep a stack of indexes still waiting for an answer, with values decreasing from bottom to top. Each new value pops and answers every smaller value on top. Only push during the first lap.

explain.intuition:
In a straight array, keep a stack of positions still waiting for a bigger value. Their values are decreasing from bottom to top, because a bigger value would already have answered the smaller ones below it. When a new value arrives, it pops and answers every waiting position with a smaller value. Each index is pushed once and popped once.

The ring only adds one thing: a position near the end may find its answer near the start. So walk the array twice. The second lap does not push anything new; it only gives the positions still on the stack their wrap-around answer. Whatever is still waiting after two laps has nothing bigger anywhere, and keeps -1.
steps: Fill ans with -1 and start with an empty stack of indexes.
For k from 0 to 2n − 1, let i = k % n.
While the stack is not empty and nums[top] < nums[i]: pop top and set ans[top] = nums[i].
pitfalls: Doing only one pass, so values near the end never see the start of the array.
Popping on <=. Equal values are not greater; [5, 5, 5] must stay all -1.
Keeping values on the stack instead of indexes. When a value is popped you then cannot tell which slot of ans to fill, especially with duplicates.

solutions.title: Walk forward from every position
solutions.idea: For each i, step through the next n − 1 positions around the ring and stop at the first bigger value.

solutions.title: Monotonic stack over two laps
solutions.idea: Keep indexes waiting for an answer on a decreasing stack. Walk the ring twice so wrap-around answers are found; push only in the first lap.

followups: Return the distance (number of steps around the ring) to the next bigger value instead of the value itself.
Answer the same question for the previous bigger value, walking backwards around the ring.
